comments.author: hammadkhaliq-del
comments.body: Thanks for the detailed report and the full traceback, that made this easy to trace. The crash happens in RoutedExperts.weight_loader in routed_experts.py, where it indexes into a parameter that has shape (0, ...) in dimension 0. That's almost certainly the w13_g_idx/w2_g_idx placeholder (or qzeros when has_zp=False) that MoeWNA16Method.create_weights deliberately creates as empty, since GPTQ doesn't actually use it. Normally there's a wrapped loader (moe_wna16_weight_loader) that's supposed to skip those names before they ever get indexed. I dug through the history and found a commit on vllm-project/vllm main, e7d0fcbc0 (July 1), that changes the call in load_weights from self.weight_loader(...) to param.weight_loader(...). That distinction matters here: param.weight_loader is what actually calls the wrapped, guarded loader; self.weight_loader calls the generic unwrapped one and skips the guard entirely. So if your build predates that commit, this would explain the crash pretty directly. That said, I want to flag something rather than assume it: your version string is 0.1.dev18302+gdfe7b7bad, which points to commit dfe7b7bad (the g is just git's own prefix marker, not part of the hash). I can't find that commit anywhere in vllm-project/vllm's main history. Given you mentioned building with MI100/gfx908 support "gated on," I suspect you're building from a fork or downstream branch rather than vanilla main, so I can't directly confirm whether it includes e7d0fcbc0 or not. Would you be able to confirm what repo/branch your Docker image is actually built from? And if you get a chance, testing against a fresh vllm-project/vllm main checkout (post July 1) would tell us pretty quickly whether this is already fixed upstream or whether there's still a real bug to chase down.

comments.author: hammadkhaliq-del
comments.body:
> It works after I merge into the current main branch! Thanks a lot. BTW, how can that commit pass the test?

I'm happy that it is fixed for you!
As for how it slipped past CI, I'm honestly not 100% sure, but my guess is it just needs a pretty specific setup to trigger: a GPTQ MoE checkpoint that falls back to WNA16 kernels, and one that actually ships g_idx (or qzeros when has_zp=False) weight files. If the existing MoE quant tests don't happen to cover that exact combo, the broken line would just sit there unused until someone loaded a real checkpoint shaped like yours.
Might be worth a quick look at tests/quantization/ or tests/kernels/moe/ to see if that fallback + g_idx/qzeros case is actually tested. If not, adding one referencing this issue would be a nice way to make sure it doesn't come back.
Since this turns out to already be fixed on main by e7d0fcbc0, I think this one can be closed. Thanks for jumping on the repro so quickly!
